messages:
edr-bot: ALERT: EDR detected suspicious autorun + outbound beaconing from 'marco-laptop' (user: marco). Threat score 78. Evidence: child process chain 'powershell.exe' -> 'curl.exe' contacting 54.210.23.17:8080. Persisted via HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\{random}. URL: https://edr.internal/alerts/1837654321 :eyes:
marco: confirmed, I'm at lunch. laptop still online on corp-wifi. can't access right now.
tania: tagging @oncall-sre — do we isolate the host or block the IP first?
oncall-sre: isolate host from network, snapshot and collect EDR artifacts. block outbound IP at firewall. also collect open processes + scheduled tasks.
edr-bot: isolation command executed by Tania: `edr isolate --host marco-laptop --reason "suspected beacon"` - network interface disabled, agent heartbeat still alive.
marco: thanks, I can jump on a call in 15m if needed.
tania: pulled live process list: `powershell.exe -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -EncodedCommand ...` and a scheduled task 'sys-update' created at 09:02 that runs PowerShell. reg query returned: `HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\sys-upd    REG_SZ    C:\\Users\\marco\\AppData\\Roaming\\sys-upd.exe`.
oncall-sre: ok block 54.210.23.17 at perimeter, add egress deny. please pull the auth logs for any AWS/KMS calls from marco before 09:00. we need to know if any long-term keys were used.
jess: FYI marco had a personal GCP service account key in %USERPROFILE%\\.config yesterday per support ticket; IT to confirm whether that key had access to prod.
it-helpdesk: opening ticket INC-2482 to track asset quarantine and user follow-up. asking Marco to power down until cleared?
marco: I do have a personal key but it's in my home dir not on C:, AFAIK not used for prod. I pushed earlier today though — could be bad.
oncall-sre: treat as potential credential exposure. start immediate rotations for any service account keys that were present on the device. We should assume secrets in user profile may be exfil'd.
tania: grabbed EDR network capture (pcap) and uploaded to secure bucket: s3://sec-artifacts/1837654321.pcap (accessed only by sec team). 
edr-bot: IOC extraction: domains: badchannelyz[.]com, 54.210.23.17; file hash: sha256:3b7f...c2a1. Yara match: Suspicious-PowerShell-Loader.
jess: can we confirm whether any infra API keys were used from the host? marco, did you have AWS CLI creds in %USERPROFILE%\\.aws\\credentials?
marco: no, I use role-based access via corp laptop normally. but I did have a local AWS creds file for a demo last week — might still be there.
oncall-sre: assume compromise. Rotate/disable any keys tied to Marco immediately. Trigger org-wide anomaly watch for the IoC.
it-helpdesk: Marco's manager notified. arranging temporary loaner laptop.
tania: removing persistence entries and quarantining identified files: `del C:\\Users\\marco\\AppData\\Roaming\\sys-upd.exe` and `schtasks /Delete /TN sys-update /F`. collecting registry hives for offline analysis.
edr-bot: post-scan: no lateral movement detected. no other hosts with this exact IOC as of now (last scan run across corp endpoint fleet).
jess: next steps: 1) rotate credentials 2) validate KMS/HSM key usage logs 3) reimage device or issue loaner 4) follow-up user interview and phishing check.
oncall-sre: agree. also file CVE triage if malware leverages a known vuln. Triage owners: marcos-app-team for any infra creds, sec for forensic.
it-helpdesk: created remediation checklist in ticket INC-2482 and scheduled reimage for 2024-11-05 14:00 UTC.
marco: appreciate everyone. i'll be available during the reimage window.
tania: closing loop here — will attach final forensic report to the ticket when analysis completes. :thumbsup:
